summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, type II diabetes, and chronic heart failure was admitted for a right second toe amputation due to wet gangrene from a nonhealing ulcer. He was admitted directly from vascular surgery clinic, started on broad-spectrum antibiotics, and underwent hemodialysis followed by an uncomplicated amputation. He recovered well in the postoperative period with no complications, was transitioned to oral pain medication and levofloxacin, and was discharged home on postoperative day one. He was instructed to resume all home medications, monitor the surgical site for signs of infection, and follow up in one month for suture removal.
problems: Ulcer of other part of foot
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
Other specified forms of chronic ischemic heart disease
Coronary atherosclerosis of unspecified type of vessel, native or graft
Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
Atrophic gastritis, without mention of hemorrhage
